items.headline: Baramulla men acquitted after six years under UAPA
items.text: A J&K special UAPA court acquitted two men held since 2020 over an alleged grenade recovery, calling the evidence inconsistent. Police had said arms were found at a highway checkpoint.

photo.alt: A long suspension footbridge with metal railings stretching into thick fog.
photo.caption: A suspension footbridge in Baramulla on a foggy morning, in 2023.

items.headline: UP told to trace bailed prisoners still jailed
items.text: In 20 UP districts, 106 of 264 undertrials granted bail remain jailed over surety conditions. The Supreme Court ordered the state to identify such prisoners in 55 more districts and secure their release.

photo.alt: A domed red and cream building with an Indian flag, behind trees and a black statue on a pedestal.
photo.caption: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi, which issued the order, in 2019.

items.headline: Maharashtra churches cancel or limit children's Bible camps
items.text: Some churches cancelled or limited Diwali Bible camps to Christian children after nine FIRs followed prayer-meeting disruptions and a new anti-conversion law. No police or government response was reported.

photo.alt: A tall cream church building with a cross on its gable, arched windows and steps up to a covered entrance.
photo.caption: St Gonsalo Garcia Church in Vasai, a town where five of the nine FIRs were filed; it is not among the churches named in the report. Photo from 2017.

items.headline: Group flags high voter deletions in Karnataka seats
items.text: A Muslim community body said 27.59% of voters were deleted in 10 Karnataka seats held by Muslim MLAs during the revision, against 19.45% statewide. No Election Commission response was reported.

photo.alt: Men, women and children stand in a queue on the veranda of an old school building used as a polling booth.
photo.caption: Voters queue at a polling booth in Bengaluru during the 2014 general election.

items.headline: Steel plant blast kills 17 workers in Turkey
items.text: An explosion at the Habaş iron and steel plant in Aliağa killed at least 17 workers and injured 12, officials said. The governor said a crane collapsed during furnace maintenance.

photo.alt: A hillside view over a coastal town and harbour, with industrial plants and chimneys on the far shore.
photo.caption: Aliağa on the Aegean coast north of İzmir, with its industrial zone behind, in 2007.

items.headline: Thirteen migrants die as boat sinks off Crete
items.text: At least 13 people died when a migrant boat sank off Crete; the coastguard rescued 18, all Sudanese. Authorities said the boat had likely been at sea for days in strong winds.

photo.alt: A marina full of white yachts in front of the low buildings of a port city under a blue sky.
photo.caption: The port of Heraklion, Crete's main city, in 2019.

items.headline: Harare demolitions leave families who bought plots homeless
items.text: Council records list over 5,000 Harare houses facing demolition under 37 court orders; residents say they bought plots through council processes. The council says it is enforcing planning rules.

photo.alt: Dry grass and a railway line in the foreground, with the high-rise skyline of a city behind.
photo.caption: Harare's skyline seen from Chiremba Road, in 2020.

items.headline: Russia's Novaya Gazeta closes after eviction
items.text: Novaya Gazeta held its final editorial meeting on Monday and closed after being evicted from its offices. The Kremlin called the closure part of "a standard rotational process".

photo.alt: The lit entrance of a pale office building at night, with a barrier and a person walking on the path.
photo.caption: Novaya Gazeta's office building on Potapovsky Lane, Moscow, on 30 October 2026, after the eviction began.

items.headline: Macao ex-lawmaker Au Kam San jailed 12.5 years
items.text: A Macao court sentenced democracy activist Au Kam San under the national security law after a closed trial. The court says he worked with hostile overseas groups; HRW calls the charges baseless.

photo.alt: A pedestrian square paved in wavy black and white stones, lined with pastel colonial buildings and shoppers.
photo.caption: Senado Square in central Macao, in 2010.

items.headline: Two still missing after Gaza tent landslide
items.text: Two people remain missing after Sunday's sandbank collapse that killed five in Deir el-Balah. Save the Children says Israel has blocked caravans promised under the ceasefire; no Israeli response was reported.

photo.alt: People in dark clothing stand among plastic-sheet tents in heavy rain on muddy ground.
photo.caption: Flooded tents of displaced Palestinians after heavy rain in Deir el-Balah, Gaza, in 2025.
photo.credit: Ashraf Amra / UNRWA, via Wikimedia Commons

items.headline: Lawyer: army should not hold ICC suspect Haroun
items.text: Sudanese lawyer Muaz Hadra said police and courts, not the army, should hold Ahmed Haroun, who faces war-crimes charges at home and an ICC warrant. No army comment was reported.

photo.alt: Rooftops and a street with parked cars in a town, with tall granite domes of mountains behind.
photo.caption: The centre of Kassala, eastern Sudan, where his lawyers say he was detained, in 2008.

focus.title: Preventive detention in Jammu & Kashmir: what the courts are finding
focus.dek: A Baramulla court acquitted two men after six years in jail under the UAPA, finding police evidence unreliable; the High Court keeps quashing PSA detentions. The administration cites "established peace".
focus.alt: A long suspension footbridge with metal railings stretching into thick fog.
